title: A review 20 years in the making! Was it worth the wait? #Wicked #Wick...
transcript: If you want an unbiased, spoiler free review of wicked from someone who actually paid for their ticket, here you go. So I went into wicked very skeptical. I honestly was not sold on this whole two part concept. I didn't know that it could work, and I'm happy to say that for the most part, I was wrong. I actually think this works really well. There are definitely some scenes that, like, you can feel they're like, trying to really stretch it out. But there are also other scenes that are just given this room to breathe that they don't have in the stage show because the stage musical is so fast paced and they just kind of go from one thing to the next to the next to the next. One of the benefits of turning this into two parts is that you don't have to rush to get to the next scene. You can actually let the scenes breathe a little bit. I think this is especially true of the Asdas ballroom scene with Glinda and Elphaba. That scene was so well done and genuinely made me emotional. If there is a drawback to this two part structure, though, it's that while Glinda and Elphaba themselves have fully realized arcs with beginning middles and ends, a lot of the side characters really don't. When it comes to characters like Bach, Nessa, Doctor Dillamond, we really don't get much from them that wasn't already in the stage show. Even with Fiera, while we do get a little bit more of him and Alpha, but I did feel like they could have given us a little bit more to just flesh out his character. But on the flip side, the heart of this film really is Glinda and Alpha, but. And their friendship. And in that sense, they really deliver. I mean, Ariana Grande and Cynthia Erivo are both perfectly cast. I have seen a lot of buzz around Ariana Grande, and rightfully so. I think her comedic timing especially impressed me. And I loved how she was able to take the larger than life Glinda that we know from the stage version and tone it down for film while still keeping the essence of the character. But for me, the true standout was Cynthia Erivo as Elphaba. Like, obviously we know vocally, she's amazing, like her wizard and I, for me, was the highlight of the film. But her acting, like, she broke my heart so many times. It really got me invested in the character of Alpha in a way that I never really have been before. And so, in my mind, the one thing the movie absolutely needed to get right in, Glinda and Alpha, it totally nailed. A couple other things I'll mention is that they made a really big deal about the live vocals, but in the actual film, a lot of the vocals sounded really processed to me, and I kind of wish They just let the raw vocals be. The only thing I'll say is that going into it there was this concern about it over reliance on CGI. While there are definitely CGI shots, for the most part this film feels really practical. I do think that all the time they spent building these physical sets really did pay off because it made the world feel so much more real and tangible. I also loved all of the little nods to The Wizard of Oz throughout. Some of them are really subtle, some of them are not so subtle, but you could really feel how much love and passion the people working on this film have for the source material and for Oz. Those are all my non spoiler thoughts. I'm gonna post a full spoiler video later this week once more people have had a chance to see it. But if you are on the fence at all, I highly recommend checking out this film. It is not perfect by any stretch of the imagination, but the love and care that the people making the film put into it, as well as the great central performances from Cynthia and Ariana, really do make this movie a must see in my opinion.
classificationReason: This is a review of the Wicked movie adaptation, not the stage production. Creator explicitly mentions 'wicked from someone who actually paid for their ticket' and discusses movie-specific elements like two-part structure and pacing differences from the stage show.
